newsitem.title: USA: Tosco profits hurt by weak oil product margins.
newsitem.headline: Tosco profits hurt by weak oil product margins.

text.p: Tosco Corp., one of the nation's largest independent refiners and marketers of petroleum products, said Wednesday its fourth-quarter profits fell as demand and prices for oil products remained weak.

Profits fell to $30.2 million, or 67 cents a share, for the quarter ended Dec. 31 from $33.8 million, or 90 cents a share, in the year-ago period. The decline came despite a jump in revenues to $2.76 billion from $1.89 billion.
"Tosco's fourth-quarter results were good given the generally poor conditions that existed in our markets during most of the period," Chief Executive Thomas D. O'Malley said.

"Refining and marketing margins were weak throughout the quarter due to the industry's inability to pass higher crude oil costs on to the consumer. Cold weather in the East helped Tosco's Bayway Refinery to a certain degree, but conditions on the West Coast were weak."
However, O'Malley said refining margins in 1996 improved somewhat from 1995's very low levels, and that retail margins were generally acceptable even after a slight drop.
"At present, margins are weak all across the U.S., but overall industry prospects appear more positive than they have for some time," O'Malley said.

Tosco said its revenues and asset base will grow by more than a third after the $1.4 billion purchase of the operating assets of 76 Products Co., the West Coast refining and marketing division of Unocal Corp. The deal, announced in November, strengthens Tosco's position as the nation's largest operator of company-controlled convenience stores.
Tosco, based in Stamford, Conn., also said it expects to restart its second Philadelphia area refinery early this summer when it sees an improving products market.
Tosco acquired the Trainer plant, formerly known as British Petroleum Co. Plc's Marcus Hook refinery, in February when it purchased BP's U.S. Northeast marketing and refining assets for $59 million.
Tosco's $100 million refurbishment and modernisation programme at the refinery is on schedule and on budget, it said.
Tosco's stock fell $1.125 to $90 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-morning.
